newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Lower Australia minimum wage not policy - Costello.
newsitem.headline: Lower Australia minimum wage not policy - Costello.

text.p: The Australian government did not have a policy of lowering the minimum wage, Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Tuesday, rejecting speculation the government planned to lower wages to boost employment growth.
"That's not a policy of this government to lower minimum wages. We won't be doing that," Costello told reporters after a cabinet meeting to discuss the employment situation.
"We've made it clear...our industrial relations legislation puts in place a safety net -- a minimum -- and we're happy with how that's operating," he said.
"We'll give those industrial relations changes the opportunity to work and we will assess over the course of this year how they work in practice."
Costello said cabinet had a useful discussion on the employment situation, but that no specific action had been decided.

"We've reaffirmed the importance of economic growth and getting in place the right conditions for economic growth -- the low inflation, low interest growth growth climate, the importance of getting the industrial relations system right and the importance of having the right incentives between wages and
He did not elaborate on how the incentives could changed to make them better.
Costello said the cabinet had looked at the way certain programmes could be delivered and would go away and conduct further work on these. He did not specify any particular programmes.
Costello later said he expected the unemployment rate to fall to about or a little below eight percent by the end of June 1998 from its current 8.5 percent.
